To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new buffer management policy, EDT, which can fully utilize the buffer of switches to absorb more burst traffic, and we theoretically deduce and quantitatively evaluate the sufficient conditions of packet dropping caused by burst traffic.
we propose a novel buffer management policy to alleviate the packet dropping problem caused by micro-bust traffic in data centers.
DT policy is not able to fully utilize switch buffer and EDT policy can absorb more microburst traffic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of DT policy under micro-burst traffic.
the buffer management policy in data center switches.
a fundamental problem that has been ignored by previous researches, and the results can be used as a guideline to design and implement the buffer management policy of switches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DT is unable to absorb the burst traffic, and the EDT policy can improve the performance of the DT policy.
EDT is able to absorb more micro-bust traffic than DT.
EDT policy can alleviate the packet dropping caused by micro-burst traffic and improve the performance of distributed applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EDT can be used to improve the performance of micro-burst traffic in DT-based switches, and it is also a good candidate for the buffer management policy of data center switches.
the buffer utilization can be improved significantly by EDT, and the packet dropping can be alleviated when the traffic size exceeds the free buffer size.
the buffer management policy in data center switches should take the characteristics of micro-burst traffic in distributed applications into consideration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of micro-burst traffic in data centers, the buffer utilization rate of DT policy may be very low and the fairness constraint in DT policy may lead to packet dropping.
, to fully absorb micro-burst traffic in data center switches, the buffer size and the fairness constraint need to be carefully designed.
, to improve the buffer utilization, it is necessary to temporarily relax the fairness constraint in DT policy when micro-burst traffic exists.
